cars.specification_market: Original BC3-based i20 N five-door road hatchback, selected 2021 UK 204-PS six-speed manual from Hyundai Motor UK’s 16 June 2021 specification release. Count the original i20 N road family once across years and equipment. Separate from i30 N and Veloster N; not the Indian BI3 N Line, ordinary i20, Coupe WRC, Rally1 or Rally2 racer. UK table says R-MDPS while earlier factory text says column-mounted C-MDPS, so steering assistance location and ratio are not assigned. Acceleration is also withheld: UK table says 6.2 seconds 0–62 mph, earlier text 6.7 seconds 0–100 km/h. Turning-circle 5.27-m label is ambiguous and omitted. No single curb weight is selected from the range, and no WRC minimum-weight equivalence, price or competition result is imported.
cars.summary: The i20 N earned both Top Gear’s 2021 Performance Car of the Year and overall Car of the Year awards. The award publisher’s assessment establishes the small hot hatch’s exceptional road-and-track appeal beyond its modest size and price. This original six-speed-manual road family is represented once; WRC inspiration is not a claim that the road car shares rally-car hardware or results.

sources.title: Hyundai Announces All New i20 N Prices and Specifications — 16 June 2021
sources.source_type: Original manufacturer UK production-road specification release
sources.notes: Three-page PDF, 162,677 bytes; all pages individually visually read, technical tables on indexes 0–1, disclaimer continues on index 2. Selected UK 204 PS / 150 kW six-speed manual. Normal and overboost torque with distinct operating ranges retained. Header confirms standard N Corner Carving Differential, Launch Control and rev matching. Steering R-MDPS conflicts with earlier introduction C-MDPS; assistance location unassigned. Acceleration, ambiguous turning circle, kerb-mass range, braking distance, prices and economy omitted.

sources.title: Revealed: the winners of the 2021 TopGear.com awards — i20 N awards
sources.notes: Both relevant award sections read: Performance Car of the Year and overall Car of the Year name Hyundai i20N. This supports performance significance, not a technical specification, universal superiority claim or transfer of every award to all ordinary i20 derivatives.

sources.title: Hyundai Motor unveils the all-new Hyundai i20 N — original model introduction
sources.notes: Relevant model, powertrain, chassis and road-launch sections read. Identifies a separate i20-based N road model, front-wheel power transfer and mechanical limited-slip differential, but selected attributes come from June UK specification sheet. Earlier steering C-MDPS and 6.7-second acceleration differ from UK technical sheet; conflicting fields withheld. WRC inspiration is not homologated road-car race equipment or an achievement of this production car. No full racing specification imported.
